description:
Detached ed25519 signature applied by an envelope's author at compose time. Distinct cryptographic layer from `tech.equanimi.secretariat.stamp` per AGENTS.md hard rule #4 (three-layer trust): every envelope on the wire carries an author signature (`$signature`, this record); the principal's Touch-ID-gated stamp (`$attestation`, the Stamp record) is selective. Author is typically the principal's scribe (an agent listed in `authorized_agents`); a principal can also self-sign for envelopes composed manually. Different keys mean receivers can cryptographically distinguish 'scribe-composed' from 'principal-composed' from 'Touch-ID-attested' without trusting a UI convention.

**Where it lives.** The signature record is embedded in the envelope's markdown frontmatter under the key `$signature`, alongside the optional `$attestation` block. The two fields coexist independently — a stamped envelope carries both; an ambient signed-only envelope carries only `$signature`.

**Canonical preimage.** Identical to the stamp's: SHA-256 over the canonical body (`docHash`), formatted `sha256:<hex>`, and the ed25519 signature is over the raw 32 bytes of that hash. Reusing the hash means the same body bytes drive both signature and stamp — and a tamper to the body breaks both layers.

**Optional in lexicon, mandatory in practice on the wire.** The field is `optional` in this lexicon to permit legacy back-compat for envelopes from before the substrate-for-themia slice. Post-slice envelopes MUST carry `$signature`; receivers may quarantine signature-missing envelopes per channel policy.

signer.description: DID of the author. For a scribe-signed envelope this is the agent's `did:key`; for a principal-self-signed envelope this is the principal's DID. Receivers resolve the DID to a verifying key (via `did:key` embedding or hosted `did:web` document) and check the signature against it. When the author is an agent, the receiver additionally verifies the agent is authorized by the claimed principal via the latest `tech.equanimi.secretariat.agentManifest` (the verifier chain from `docs/pitches/2026-05-21-substrate-for-themia.md`).

signerRole.description: Role of the author at signing time. `agent` = an authorized non-principal DID (today's only role: scribe). `principal` = the principal themselves signed at compose (e.g. CLI compose without a scribe configured). Receiver-side hint for UI distinction; the cryptographic check still relies on `signer` + the agent-manifest chain.

docHash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical body of the signed document, formatted as `sha256:<hex>`. Same canonicalization rules as `tech.equanimi.secretariat.stamp.docHash`: strip leading BOM, normalize CRLF→LF, strip trailing whitespace. The hash field is duplicated between `$signature` and `$attestation` (when both present); they MUST agree, otherwise the envelope is tampered.

signedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of signing. Distinct from the stamp's `stampedAt` — `signedAt` is when the author committed the body bytes; `stampedAt` is when the principal elevated the envelope to authoritative.

signature.description: Detached ed25519 signature over the raw 32 bytes of `docHash`. Format: `ed25519:<base64>` with 64 raw bytes. Matches the stamp's signature shape so the same `Signature` value object round-trips both layers.
